items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: But I had my group, Jimmy Jones on piano, and Harold Jones on drums and Jim [Hewitt] bass, and we went out and we played.

ctx.x: Now, in the meantime there came the bebop era when all the piano players were playing the bebop era. But Errol was Errol. Dizzy was Dizzy. You understand what I'm getting at. And I enjoy hearing them just as much now as I did then. You know, I played a concert last night with my little group, and the first part of the program was devoted to young black musicians, and they had the youth band and they graduated to some, you know, a little older, and they'd have another group, and it was nice.

But I had my group, Jimmy Jones on piano, and Harold Jones on drums and Jim [Hewitt] bass, and we went out and we played. And the response was resounding. So after we finished I went to the dressing room and everyone, the kids and the older musicians, said, oh, that was just so beautiful. And I looked over there and sitting on the couch was Marshall Royal, who was going to appear with the [pier] band that came on later. And it occurred to me we have to show the kids.

I looked at Marshall and I said now here's a great saxophone player, this is -- we have to -- and I said this to Marshall, I said, well Marshall, you know, we old timers really have to do something for the kids. He said, that's right. You know, because it's timeless, you know. You don't grow old musically. I don't think so. I know better.

items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: So John, he was asking me, 'Would you like to make it with me with this [quartet]?' Before he finished the question I said yes.
